newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to apologize to victims in syphilis study.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to apologize to victims in syphilis study.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will apologise to a group of black men in Tuskegee, Alabama whose syphilis went untreated for years as part of a federal study, the White House said on Tuesday.
"We think by doing a public apology like this, it makes certain these sorts of things will never happen again," said White House spokeswoman Mary Ellen Glynn.

In a medical research project conducted by the government in Tuskegee that began in 1932 and lasted for 40 years, 600 African-American men infected with syphilis were left untreated, even though penicillin became available during the study and was found effective against the disease.
Eight of the human guinea pigs involved in the Tuskegee project are still alive, the youngest of whom is 87 years old.

Clinton, who previously apologised to Americans who were unknowingly involved in government radiation experiments that took place years before he became president, will express his regret to the Tuskegee group at a public ceremony sometime in the near future, Glynn said.
